text:
Predicates:
Likes(x, y) ::: x likes y.
Bark(x) ::: x is an animal that barks.
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog.
Jump(x) ::: x is an animal that jumps.
Legs(x) ::: x has legs.
Terricolous(x) ::: x is terricolous.
Premises:
∀x (Bark(x) → ¬Likes(jane, x)) ::: Jane does not like any animals that bark.
∀x (Dog(x) → Bark(x)) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀x (Jump(x) → Likes(jane, x)) ::: Jane likes all animals that jump.
∀x (Legs(x) → Jump(x)) ::: If an animal has legs, then it jumps.
∀x (Terricolous(x) → Legs(x)) ::: If an animal is terricolous, then it has legs.
Animal(kiki) ::: KiKi is an animal.
(¬Jump(kiki) ∧ ¬Legs(kiki)) → (Terricolous(kiki) ∨ Legs(kiki)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.
Conclusion:
Dog(kiki) ∧ Bark(kiki) ::: KiKi is a barking dog.
